candidates: When a TypeScript function accepts a destructured config/options parameter that callers may partially specify, assign defaults at the property level (e.g., `{ depth = 2, clobber = false }`) and mark those properties optional in the TypeScript type (e.g., `{ depth?: number; clobber?: boolean }`). A whole-object default (`= {}`) only kicks in when the argument is entirely omitted — it does NOT merge missing fields from a partially-provided object, leaving unspecified properties as `undefined`.

Do not use both destructuring property-level defaults and `Object.assign` to apply the same defaults to the same parameter — they are redundant. Choose one approach; prefer destructuring defaults in TypeScript code.
